Metadata.title: Practise derivatives — differentiation rules | __DOMAIN__
Metadata.description: Practise derivatives and differentiation rules — free and adaptive. Power rule, product rule, quotient rule, chain rule, trigonometry, exponentials and logarithms. Perfect for exam preparation.

Home.lead: Adaptive exercises for differentiation. Start immediately, get instant feedback, and for every mistake the site explains exactly what went wrong, with a follow-up question tailored to that mistake.
Home.subLead: You work through exercises chapter by chapter, get an explanation for every mistake, and see exactly where you stand under Progress. Ready for the test? Build your own practice test under Self-test. <howItWorks>How it works</howItWorks>.
Home.feature1Body: No long explanatory videos. You learn derivatives by working through them and getting explanations for every mistake.
Home.feature2Body: The site tracks your pace. You get more of what you find difficult, less of what you already know.
Home.feature3Body: Notation and learning progression follow a logical order. From the power rule to the chain rule.
Home.topicsIntro: All differentiation rules for high school calculus, in increasing difficulty:
Home.topic1Body: The foundation. From xⁿ to n·xⁿ⁻¹, including negative and fractional exponents.
Home.topic3Body: For functions like (x² + 1)·sin(x). Two parts each separately, then combine.
Home.topic4Body: For fractions like (x² + 1) / (x − 3). Only when the product rule is not easier.
Home.topic5Body: For composite functions like sin(3x²). Bring in the inner function's derivative.
Home.topic6Body: sin, cos, ln, e, and rational functions. Having these ready is half the battle.
Home.how1Body: For example: find the derivative of f(x) = 3x² + 2x − 5. You type your answer using a math keyboard.
Home.how2Body: Correct? On to the next one. Wrong? The site explains which rule you should have used, works through the steps, and shows exactly where your answer went wrong.
Home.how3Body: Based on your mistake you get an exercise that addresses exactly that type of problem. So you fix the gap instead of ignoring it.
Home.how4Body: When you answer a topic correctly several times in a row, the site marks it as mastered. You'll see it less often after that.
Home.ctaBody: Create a free account and practice your first fifty derivatives today. No credit card. No limit.
Home.faq1A: Yes, completely free. Create an account and start practising immediately. No ads, no trial subscription.
Home.faq2A: For students who need to practise differentiation rules. The site covers the power rule, sum rule, product rule, quotient rule, chain rule, and standard derivatives (sin, cos, ln, e).
Home.faq3A: All differentiation rules for high school calculus: power rule, sum and difference rule, constant factor rule, product rule, quotient rule, and chain rule. Plus standard derivatives of sine, cosine, exponential and logarithmic functions.
Home.faq4Q: How does the adaptive approach work?
Home.faq4A: The site tracks per topic how well you master it. Exercises you find difficult appear more often; topics you already know appear less often. For every mistake the site explains exactly what went wrong and gives you a fitting follow-up question to fix it.
Home.faq5Q: Is this suitable for exam preparation?
Home.faq5A: Absolutely. Derivatives are the foundation for large parts of the calculus exam (extrema, tangent lines, dynamic models). By becoming fluent here you'll work through the other parts of the exam faster and with fewer mistakes.
Home.faq6Q: Is this only for Dutch students?
Home.faq6A: The exercises were originally written in Dutch, but the theory and all interface text are available in English. The mathematical content is of course universal.

HoeHetWerkt.title: How it works
HoeHetWerkt.description: Practise chapter by chapter, build your own self-test, follow your progress and ask a question: this is how __DOMAIN__ works.
HoeHetWerkt.intro: __DOMAIN__ has one goal: to make you faster and more confident at integration. There is nothing to set up beforehand. You create a free account, pick a chapter and start. For every mistake the site explains what went wrong.
HoeHetWerkt.doenH2: What you can do on the site
HoeHetWerkt.card1Body: You pick a chapter and a topic inside it, for example standard integrals or integration by parts. The overview shows how each exercise went: green is correct, red is wrong. That way you see at a glance what still needs work.
HoeHetWerkt.card2Body: Build your own practice test: you choose the topics, the number of questions and whether you only want questions you have not done yet. You can set it so you only see the answers after the last question, just like a real test.
HoeHetWerkt.card3Body: Under Progress you see per topic how far you are: how many questions you answered, what percentage was correct, and which kinds of mistakes come up most often. Everything is saved, so you continue on your phone where you left off on your laptop.
HoeHetWerkt.card4Body: Can't work it out, not even with the theory or an explanation video? Send in your question, with a photo from your book if that is easier. You get an answer by email, and there is a good chance it becomes a video.
HoeHetWerkt.opgaveIntro: Every round of practice goes the same way:
HoeHetWerkt.step1Body: You type your answer with the maths keyboard, so fractions, roots and powers all go in properly.
HoeHetWerkt.step2Body: Correct? On to the next one. Wrong? Then you see which rule you should have used, with the steps and the exact point where your answer went off.
HoeHetWerkt.step3Title: 3. You get a matching follow-up question.
HoeHetWerkt.step3Body: After a mistake you get an exercise of exactly the same type, so you can put it right straight away instead of leaving it.
HoeHetWerkt.step4Body: Get a topic right a few times in a row and it counts as mastered, so you see it less often. If you still want an explanation, it is under Theory and in the explanation videos.
HoeHetWerkt.delenIntro: An integral exercise almost always falls apart into three pieces. Once you know which part you lose, you know what to practise. The theory and the explanations on this site follow that split.
HoeHetWerkt.deel1Title: Part 1 — from word problem to integral.
HoeHetWerkt.deel1Body: You translate the text into the right integral: “the region between the graph of f, the x-axis and the lines x = 1 and x = p” becomes the integral of f from 1 to p.
HoeHetWerkt.deel2Body: Which standard form is this, and which route goes with it: antidifferentiate directly, substitution, or integration by parts? This part is in every exercise.
HoeHetWerkt.deel3Title: Part 3 — doing something with the result.
HoeHetWerkt.deel3Body: Solving an equation, finding p, rounding. In a bare “compute exactly” exercise parts 1 and 3 drop out and only part 2 is left.
HoeHetWerkt.delenVoorbeeld: Take f(x) = 3x² and the question: for which p is the region between the graph, the x-axis and the lines x = 1 and x = p equal to 26? Part 1: that is the integral of 3x² from 1 to p. Part 2: an antiderivative of 3x² is x³, so the result is p³ − 1. Part 3: solve p³ − 1 = 26, so p³ = 27 and p = 3.
HoeHetWerkt.weten1: Everything on the site is free. You do need an account, otherwise the site cannot save your progress.
HoeHetWerkt.weten2: Notation and order follow the Dutch Getal & Ruimte method. If you use another method, the site works just as well.
HoeHetWerkt.weten3: You can stop whenever you like. After logging back in your answers and your progress are still there.

Theorie.title: Differentiation: all rules on one page
Theorie.description: All differentiation rules for high school calculus on one page: power rule, sum rule, product rule, quotient rule, chain rule, exponential, trigonometry and ln. With examples and steps.
Theorie.h1: Differentiation: all rules on one page
Theorie.intro: A reference for all the differentiation rules you'll encounter in calculus. Per topic you see the formula, a worked example and, when you expand it, explanation and steps. You can also go straight to <practiceLink>practice</practiceLink>.
Theorie.noTheory: No theory for this section yet, exercises only.
Theorie.methodeIntro: Elke afgeleide bereken je met hetzelfde stappenplan. Stap 0 is de enige echte beslissing: kijk naar de buitenste schil en kies de regel. Daarna zijn stap 1, 2 en 3 altijd hetzelfde. Klik op een regel om te zien wat je in elke stap doet; bij de hoofdstukken links zie je de methode toegepast op voorbeelden.
Theorie.schemaStap0Generic: Welk teken scheidt de grootste delen van de functie? Een + of −, een ·, een breukstreep, of een macht om haakjes. Dat teken bepaalt de regel.
Theorie.schemaGeneric1: Stel de onderdelen vast: g en h, of buitenkant en kern.
Theorie.schemaGeneric2: Bereken hun afgeleides. Vraagt een deel een andere regel? Dan noem je dat deel even f en begin je ervoor opnieuw bij stap 1.
Theorie.schemaGeneric3: Vul de formule van de regel in.
Theorie.toonGenest: Hoe kom ik aan deze afgeleide?
